Bathroom remodeling project completed in the Houston area, featuring a modern walk-in shower, marble-look tile, glass shower enclosure, updated vanity, new flooring, and coordinated wall tile throughout the space. This type of bathroom renovation focuses on improving both the appearance and daily functionality of one of the most used areas in the home. The shower area includes large-format marble-look wall tile, a decorative accent band, built-in shower niches, a hexagon mosaic shower floor, and a frameless-style glass enclosure. These details help create a cleaner, brighter, and more open bathroom layout while maintaining a polished residential finish. The tile design continues through the floor and lower wall areas, giving the room a consistent and updated look. Bathroom remodeling projects in Houston homes often include shower reconstruction, waterproofing preparation, tile installation, plumbing fixture updates, vanity installation, lighting improvements, ventilation, and finish work. In this project, the white and gray color palette helps make the room feel more spacious while allowing the tile pattern and glass shower enclosure to become the main design features. A renovation like this is commonly used to replace older bathroom layouts, improve shower access, update worn finishes, and create a more modern interior style. The finished bathroom combines practical surfaces, clean lines, and coordinated materials for a refreshed residential space.

Black shingles on a red brick home, it's one of those combinations that just works every single time. The contrast is sharp, the look is timeless, and once it's up, it's hard to imagine the house looking any other way. This is Tamko Heritage in Weathered Wood Black, installed on a classic brick ranch with a covered porch that wraps the full front of the home. The low-slope roofline on a house like this needs to be done with care, every valley, every transition point around the chimney, every vent penetration has to be sealed and flashed correctly or you'll find out about it the hard way down the road. Everything was done right on this one. Clean edges, proper ventilation, and a finished product that sits perfectly against the brick and white trim. Shingle roof replacement on an older brick home takes a little more attention to detail than a standard job, and that's exactly the kind of work we take seriously. We handle residential roof replacements throughout Southern Illinois, from straightforward jobs to the ones that need a little extra care.

From the owner
Most people have a friend they call when they need advice. A mechanic friend before buying a used car. A doctor friend when a medical issue comes up. An attorney friend before signing important documents. But what happens when someone gives you a $20,000, $50,000, or $100,000 remodeling estimate? Most homeowners don’t have a contractor friend. So they are forced to make decisions on their own. They trust online reviews. They trust a website. They trust what the salesperson tells them. Sometimes it works out. Sometimes it doesn’t. Over the years, I’ve met many homeowners who told me the same thing: “I wish I had someone knowledgeable to look at this before I signed.” That’s exactly why we created our Remodel Audit service. Think of it as having a contractor friend or family member who understands construction and can help you make better decisions. Someone who can look at an estimate and tell you: • Does this price make sense? • Is anything important missing? • Are there hidden costs that may appear later? • Is the contractor using the right materials? • Are they following proper waterproofing and preparation procedures? • Are they protecting your home from dust and damage? • Are they doing quality work? • Are there any red flags? The best part? You do NOT have to hire us. If another contractor is doing the work, that’s perfectly fine. Our goal is simple: To help homeowners avoid expensive mistakes and make informed decisions before, during, and after a pro

From the owner
A homeowner in Spring called us after a slow roof leak had been repaired by a roofer — but the interior still felt off. No standing water, no active drip. Just a faint odor and one wall that had developed a slight discoloration near the ceiling line. Here is what we found: The roofer had done the right thing on the exterior. The penetration was sealed. But no one had assessed the interior after the fact. Moisture readings on the wall framing behind the discolored drywall came back significantly elevated. The leak had been slow and intermittent over what appeared to be several weeks — enough to saturate the insulation in the wall cavity and raise moisture in the framing to a level that mold growth was likely without intervention. We documented the affected zone, removed the compromised drywall section, extracted the saturated insulation, and ran the framing through a structured drying protocol over four days. Final readings confirmed dry standard. No mold colony had fully established — the call came early enough. The homeowner's takeaway: a repaired roof does not mean a dry interior. The exterior fix and the interior drying are separate scopes. If you have had a roof repair and your interior has not been assessed for moisture, that gap is worth closing. Contact SGM Services.
